summary.text: 得 means “obtain” or “get.” Its early forms are interpreted as a hand taking a shell. The received graph is traditionally analyzed with 彳 for movement and 㝵 as a sound element; the shell’s name and the sound match remain unresolved.

formation.text: The received graph is phonosemantic in the Shuowen analysis: 彳 contributes movement, while 㝵 is assigned a phonetic role. Separately, early forms are interpreted as a hand taking a shell to express obtaining. The phonetic role is explicit in the traditional analysis, though a paired historical pronunciation for 㝵 and 得 has not been verified.

components.text: 彳 is associated with movement in the traditional analysis of 得 and is associated with 行. The evidence does not establish it as 行’s full-form counterpart in this character.

The Shuowen tradition assigns 㝵 the sound role in 得 and associates it with “take.” Later shapes resembling 目, 日, or 旦, and a seal form resembling 見, are also described; their relation to this component is unsettled.

sound_limitation.text: A component-specific reading for 㝵/䙷 paired with 得 has not been verified. 得 is reconstructed as *tˤək in the Baxter–Sagart system and *tɯːɡ in the Zhengzhang system, but these host readings do not establish the component’s pronunciation.

history.text: Early forms are interpreted as a hand taking a shell. The curated oracle-style drawing represents this interpretation; it is a modern redraw, and the shell-like element does not establish the object’s original name or pronunciation.

Later forms are described as changing the hand element 又 to 寸 and reshaping 貝 toward forms resembling 目, 日, or 旦. A received seal form resembling 見 is described as a possible corruption of 貝. The full sequence is not confirmed by a continuous series of dated forms.
The Shuowen tradition analyzes 得 as 彳 plus phonetic 㝵. Variant dictionaries connect 䙷 and 㝵 as old or alternative forms, without establishing the complete chronology of the graph’s shapes.

uncertainties.text: The earliest character-specific attestation and its date remain unresolved. The hand-and-shell account explains the proposed graphic meaning but does not establish the shell’s original name or pronunciation.
It remains unclear how the early hand-and-shell picture relates to the later 彳-plus-㝵 analysis, or when 㝵 took on the phonetic role assigned to it in the Shuowen tradition.
A reported comparison with Tibetan thub is unverified. The chronology of extended and grammatical uses is disputed.

senses.period: Dating unresolved; attested in Warring States manuscript examples
senses.text: The hand-taking-shell interpretation presents obtaining as the graph’s proposed original sense, though the earliest securely dated attestation is unresolved. Warring States manuscript examples use 得 to mean “obtain” or “get” by that period.

senses.gloss: meet, use, understand, finish, suffice, reach, be able; auxiliary and particle functions
senses.period: Historical; individual developments and dates unresolved
senses.text: These meanings and grammatical uses are recorded, but their order and development from “obtain” are not established. One study argues that pre-Qin examples still mean “obtain” and that auxiliary use had not yet developed; other descriptions place a possibility use earlier, leaving the chronology disputed.
Modern usage includes “obtain,” “get,” “gain,” and “acquire.” These meanings alone do not show when or how the other historical uses developed.

limitations.text: No dated sequence links “obtain” to the listed extended and grammatical uses, so no specific semantic transitions are asserted.
The reported relationship with Tibetan thub does not establish borrowing, cognacy, direction, or sound correspondences.

overview.text: 得 means “obtain” or “get.” Early forms are interpreted as a hand taking a shell. In the traditional analysis of the received graph, 彳 suggests movement and 㝵 supplies sound, though their historical sound match has not been verified.

components.text: 彳 contributes movement in the traditional analysis and is associated with 行; its role here as a side form of 行 is not established.
The Shuowen tradition gives 㝵 a sound role, but no paired historical reading for it and 得 has been verified.

relationships.text: In the Shuowen analysis of 得, 彳 contributes the idea of movement.
The Shuowen analysis explicitly assigns 㝵 a sound role in 得. This is a traditional phonetic analysis; no paired reconstruction establishes the component-to-character pronunciation match.
